jd:
Platform / DevOps engineer
Mid
Product-led SaaS company moving shared data stores onto managed cloud databases. A small platform team owns OpenTofu modules so feature teams can request Postgres without clicking through the DigitalOcean UI. Hiring to strengthen day-to-day IaC for managed databases and safe plan-before-apply habits.

Day to day:
- Author and review OpenTofu for DigitalOcean managed databases and related cloud resources
- Keep provider versions and variables clear so others can init and plan the same stack
- Validate changes with tofu plan before anyone applies to shared accounts
- Pair with backend engineers on “what would this create?” reviews of database sizing and region choices
- Improve shared templates and conventions for managed Postgres on DigitalOcean

Required skills:
- Comfortable writing OpenTofu (or Terraform-compatible) HCL with required_providers and provider blocks
- Can declare a DigitalOcean managed Postgres cluster (digitalocean_database_cluster with engine pg)
- Can pass a DigitalOcean API token via variable or environment without committing secrets
- Can run tofu init and tofu plan and interpret a create plan

Nice to have:
- Familiarity with DigitalOcean database size slugs and regions
- Experience with remote state backends and workspaces
- Prior work on internal platform or developer-experience IaC modules
- Knowledge of database firewalls, replicas, or connection pooling on DigitalOcean

Constraints:
- Assessment focuses on OpenTofu that would create a managed Postgres cluster — not applying it live or operating an existing cluster
- Do not test Kubernetes, multi-cloud sprawl, or full VPC networking in this challenge
- Candidate works in a desktop environment with Terminal and OpenTofu available; they bring their own DigitalOcean API token
- Requirements on the desktop are shared scenery; do not replace the target with a different cloud or database product
prompt: Platform needs an OpenTofu root module that would create a DigitalOcean managed PostgreSQL cluster. Requirements for name, region, size, Postgres version, and node count are on your desktop. Write the configuration, authenticate with your own DigitalOcean API token, and prove it with a successful tofu plan. Do not apply.
